title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 186 (Loan and investment by company)

content.overview: Section 186 limits inter-corporate loans, guarantees, security and acquisitions. A company shall not directly or indirectly give any loan to any person or other body corporate, give any guarantee or provide security in connection with a loan, or acquire by way of subscription, purchase or otherwise the securities of any other body corporate, exceeding the higher of (a) sixty per cent of its paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium account, or (b) one hundred per cent of its free reserves and securities premium account, except with the prior approval of the company by a special resolution. Investments through more than two layers of investment companies are restricted. Interest on loans cannot be lower than the prescribed yield. Disclosure in financial statements is required. A company in default of deposits cannot use the section until the default is cured. Stated exceptions include ordinary-course lending/investment by banking, insurance and housing-finance companies, and acquisition under a rights issue.
content.glance: Ceiling = higher of 60% of (paid-up + free reserves + securities premium) or 100% of (free reserves + securities premium); special resolution to exceed; max two layers of investment companies; prescribed minimum interest; disclosure; deposit-default bar; banking/insurance/HFC and rights-issue exceptions.
content.study: Without prejudice to the provisions contained in this Act, a company shall unless otherwise prescribed, make investment through not more than two layers of investment companies. No company shall directly or indirectly (a) give any loan to any person or other body corporate; (b) give any guarantee or provide security in connection with a loan to any other body corporate or person; and (c) acquire by way of subscription, purchase or otherwise, the securities of any other body corporate, exceeding sixty per cent of its paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium account or one hundred per cent of its free reserves and securities premium account, whichever is more. Where the aggregate exceeds the limit, prior approval by special resolution is required. No loan shall be given at a rate of interest lower than the prevailing yield of one year, three year, five year or ten year Government security closest to the tenor of the loan. Every company shall disclose in the financial statement the full particulars of loans, guarantees, security and investments. A company which is in default in the repayment of any deposits or in payment of interest thereon shall not give any loan or give any guarantee or provide any security or make an acquisition till such default is subsisting. Exceptions include a loan or guarantee or security or acquisition made by a banking company or an insurance company or a housing finance company in the ordinary course of its business, and acquisition of shares pursuant to a rights issue. Distinct from the director-loan prohibition in section 185. Current-law framing: compute the ceiling; test special resolution; apply layer limit, interest floor, disclosure and deposit-default bar; check exceptions.

sections.heading: Ceiling
sections.body: Aggregate of loans, guarantees, security and acquisitions must not exceed the higher of 60% of paid-up share capital + free reserves + securities premium, or 100% of free reserves + securities premium, without prior special resolution.

sections.heading: Two-Layer Rule
sections.body: Investment through not more than two layers of investment companies, subject to prescribed exceptions.

sections.heading: Interest and Disclosure
sections.body: Loan interest not below the prescribed Government-security yield; full particulars disclosed in the financial statement.

sections.heading: Deposit-Default Bar and Exceptions
sections.body: Company in deposit default cannot use the section until default is cured. Banking, insurance and housing-finance ordinary-course transactions, and rights-issue acquisitions, are excepted.

examples.title: Exceeding the ceiling
examples.body: A company with paid-up capital, free reserves and securities premium of ₹100 crore proposes inter-corporate loans aggregating ₹70 crore. That exceeds 60% (₹60 crore). A prior special resolution is required under s. 186.

examples.title: Deposit default
examples.body: A company is in default in repayment of deposits. It cannot give a fresh inter-corporate loan under s. 186 until the default is cured.

hypotheticals.question: Does Board approval alone authorise an inter-corporate loan above the s. 186 ceiling?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Exceeding the higher of the two percentage limits requires prior approval of the company by a special resolution. Board approval is not a substitute.

distinctions.title: Inter-corporate loans/investments (s. 186) vs loan to directors (s. 185)
distinctions.left: Ceilings and special resolution for body-corporate lending/investment
distinctions.right: Prohibition focused on directors and connected persons

misconceptions.trap: Any inter-corporate loan is allowed if the Board approves it.
misconceptions.correction: Above the statutory ceiling, a prior special resolution of the company is required. Deposit-defaulting companies are barred until the default is cured.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 186 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Compute the ceiling. II. Test special resolution if exceeded. III. Apply layer, interest, disclosure and deposit-default rules. IV. Check exceptions. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Ceiling calculation; resolution status; exceptions; precise relief.
